trigger.symptom: The threaded pair ran on an oversubscribed node (see hpc_stan_threaded_pair.json).
trigger.cause: Hypothesis: the previous threaded pair was uninformative because the node was oversubscribed, so D~99 with 16 threads per chain on a whole 112-core node would show whether threading helps.

tasks.note: Threads engaged: about 23 cores per chain, 114 TBB threads per process, about 92 busy cores (observed with ps/top during the run; not re-verified). Iteration count at cancellation was not re-verified in this audit; earlier notes say fewer than 160, about the single-thread rate.

deviations.cancel_cause_as_stated_at_the_time: Throughput looked unchanged despite engaged threads; I concluded reduce_sum was deep-copying its shared arguments. That mechanism was an inference reported as a finding and is RETRACTED: the mechanism for no speed-up is unexplained.
deviations.result: No measurable throughput gain from threading at D~99 in this one clean test.
deviations.source: Slurm facts (state, elapsed, node, CPUs, submit time) come from sacct as read on 2026-10-13; cohort, host and W&B run id come from each run's W&B config. The two agree on node and duration for every job. sacct truncates the cancelling uid, so who issued each scancel is not recoverable from it; the causes below are the reasons stated at the time and are marked where they were later found wrong.

cost.progress_discarded: 3h04m of 112 CPUs on an exclusive node
